questions.question: A point has:
options: neither length nor width — just a position
questions.answer: neither length nor width — just a position
questions.explanation: A point marks a position; it has no size.

questions.question: A line:
options: extends without end in both directions
questions.answer: extends without end in both directions
questions.explanation: A line has no endpoints; it goes on forever in both directions.

questions.question: A line segment has:
questions.explanation: A line segment is a piece of a line bounded by two endpoints.

questions.question: A ray has:
questions.explanation: A ray starts at one endpoint and extends without end in the other direction.

questions.question: Which has a definite (finite) length?
questions.explanation: A line segment has two endpoints, so its length is finite. A line and a ray are infinite.

questions.question: An angle is formed by:
options: two rays sharing the same endpoint
questions.answer: two rays sharing the same endpoint
questions.explanation: Two rays meeting at a common endpoint form an angle; the shared endpoint is the vertex.

questions.question: The shared endpoint of the two rays of an angle is called the:
questions.explanation: The vertex is the corner where the two arms meet.

questions.question: In the angle ∠ABC, which letter is the vertex?
questions.explanation: By convention, the MIDDLE letter names the vertex.

questions.question: An angle has vertex P and arms going through M and N. Which is its correct name?
questions.explanation: The vertex P must be the MIDDLE letter; the other two letters can be in any order.

questions.question: Angles are measured in:
questions.explanation: The unit of angle measure is the degree (°).

questions.question: A complete (full) turn around a point measures:
questions.explanation: One full turn is 360 degrees.

questions.question: Half a turn measures:
questions.explanation: Half of 360° is 180°; this is also called a straight angle.

questions.question: A quarter turn measures:
questions.explanation: A quarter of 360° is 90°; this is a right angle.

questions.question: A protractor measures angles up to:
questions.explanation: A standard half-circle protractor goes from 0° to 180°.

questions.question: When measuring an angle with a protractor, where should the centre of the protractor be placed?
options: On the vertex of the angle
questions.answer: On the vertex of the angle
questions.explanation: The centre point of the protractor must coincide with the vertex of the angle.

questions.question: An angle that measures exactly 90° is called:
questions.explanation: An angle of exactly 90° is a right angle.

questions.question: An angle smaller than 90° is called:
questions.explanation: Acute means 'sharp' — an angle less than 90°.

questions.question: An angle between 90° and 180° is called:
questions.explanation: Obtuse means 'blunt / wide' — between 90° and 180°.

questions.question: An angle that measures exactly 180° is called:
questions.explanation: A straight angle is 180° — the two arms point in opposite directions.

questions.question: An angle between 180° and 360° is called:
questions.explanation: Reflex angles are greater than 180° but less than 360°.

questions.question: Classify an angle of 45°.
questions.explanation: 45° < 90°, so it's acute.

questions.question: Classify an angle of 120°.
questions.explanation: 120° is between 90° and 180°.

questions.question: Classify an angle of 240°.
Which angle is NOT acute?
questions.explanation: 100° is greater than 90° (obtuse). The others are all less than 90°.

questions.question: Two lines that never meet, no matter how far they are extended, are called:
questions.explanation: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet.

questions.question: Two lines that meet at exactly one point are called:
questions.explanation: Intersecting lines cross at a single point.

questions.question: Two lines that intersect at a right angle (90°) are called:
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines cross at exactly 90°.

questions.question: The two rails of a railway track are an example of:
questions.explanation: The rails stay the same distance apart — they are parallel.

questions.question: Adjacent edges of a notebook (the long side and the short side) are an example of:
questions.explanation: Adjacent edges meet at a right angle (90°).

questions.question: Two angles whose sum is 180° (and which lie on a straight line together) are called:
questions.explanation: A linear pair sums to 180°.

questions.question: When two lines intersect, the angles OPPOSITE each other are called:
questions.explanation: These pairs are equal in measure.

questions.question: Two lines intersect. One angle is 70°. The angle next to it (linear pair) is:
Two lines intersect. One angle is 70°. The angle directly opposite is:
questions.explanation: Vertically opposite angles are equal.

questions.question: Two lines cross at a point. One angle is 35°. What are the OTHER three angles?
questions.explanation: The angle opposite is 35° (vertically opposite). The two angles next to 35° (linear pairs) are 145° each.

questions.question: If two lines intersect and ALL FOUR angles are equal, each angle is:
questions.explanation: Four equal angles around an intersection: 360°/4 = 90°. The lines are perpendicular.

questions.question: Which of these would you draw to show a RIGHT angle?
options: two arms forming a straight line
questions.explanation: A right angle is exactly 90° — two arms perpendicular like the corner of a book.

questions.question: Which has NO endpoints?
questions.explanation: A line extends without end in both directions; it has no endpoints.

questions.question: Does the size of an angle depend on the LENGTHS of its arms?
options: Yes — longer arms means a bigger angle
No — only the OPENING between the arms matters
Yes — but only for right angles
questions.answer: No — only the OPENING between the arms matters
questions.explanation: The size of an angle is the rotation from one arm to the other; arm length does not affect it.

questions.question: Three quarters of a turn measures:
questions.explanation: Three quarters of 360° = 270°. Also classified as a reflex angle.

questions.question: An angle measures 95°. Which type is it?
An angle measures 178°. Which type is it?
questions.explanation: 178° is just below 180°, so it's obtuse, NOT straight (straight is exactly 180°).

questions.question: Which of these IS a right angle?
questions.explanation: A right angle is EXACTLY 90°.

questions.question: Two lines intersect. One pair of vertically opposite angles is 50° each. What is each of the OTHER pair?
questions.explanation: The other pair is the linear-pair partner: 180° − 50° = 130° each.

questions.question: If a linear pair has measures (2x)° and (3x)°, find x.
questions.explanation: 2x + 3x = 180 → 5x = 180 → x = 36. So the angles are 72° and 108°.

questions.question: A line has a definite length.
questions.explanation: A line extends without end; it does NOT have a definite (finite) length.

questions.question: In ∠XYZ, the vertex is Y.
questions.explanation: The middle letter names the vertex.

questions.question: An angle of 90° is acute.
questions.explanation: 90° is a RIGHT angle, not acute. Acute means strictly less than 90°.

questions.question: A straight angle measures 180°.
questions.explanation: Half a turn — the two arms point in opposite directions.

questions.question: Parallel lines always stay the same distance apart.
questions.explanation: By definition; otherwise they would meet somewhere.

questions.question: Vertically opposite angles are always equal.
questions.explanation: When two lines intersect, the angles directly opposite each other are equal.

questions.question: Two angles forming a linear pair always add up to 360°.
questions.explanation: A linear pair sums to 180°, not 360°.

questions.question: A ray has ____ endpoint(s).
questions.explanation: A ray has exactly one endpoint.

questions.question: In an angle ∠ABC, the vertex is letter ____.
questions.explanation: The middle letter is always the vertex.

questions.question: One full turn measures ____ degrees.
questions.explanation: Complete angle = 360°.

questions.question: An angle of exactly 90° is called a ____ angle.
questions.explanation: 90° = right angle.

questions.question: Two lines that meet at a right angle are called ____ lines.
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines meet at 90°.

questions.question: If one angle of a linear pair is 65°, the other is ____°.
Explain in your own words the difference between a LINE, a LINE SEGMENT and a RAY.
questions.answer: A line extends without end in BOTH directions and has no endpoints. A line segment is a piece of a line with TWO endpoints and a definite length. A ray has ONE endpoint and extends without end in the other direction (like a torch beam).
questions.explanation: Number of endpoints distinguishes them.

questions.question: Name the parts of an angle and explain how to name an angle using three letters.
questions.answer: An angle has a VERTEX (the corner) and two ARMS (the rays). Naming uses three letters with the vertex in the MIDDLE — e.g. ∠ABC where B is the vertex. The order of A and C does not matter.
questions.explanation: Standard three-letter convention.

questions.question: Describe the four steps of measuring an angle using a protractor.
questions.answer: (1) Place the centre of the protractor exactly on the vertex. (2) Align the 0° line of the protractor with one arm of the angle. (3) Read the degree mark where the OTHER arm crosses the protractor. (4) Use the inner or outer scale, whichever starts at 0° on your aligned arm.
questions.explanation: Standard procedure; mistakes usually come from picking the wrong scale.

questions.question: Classify each angle: (i) 25°, (ii) 90°, (iii) 135°, (iv) 200°, (v) 360°.
questions.explanation: Apply the type-by-measure rules.

questions.question: Two lines cross. One angle measures 40°. Find the other three angles, and explain the rule used.
questions.answer: The angle directly OPPOSITE 40° equals 40° (vertically opposite angles are equal). The other two angles are linear-pair partners of 40°, so they are 180° − 40° = 140° each. Three other angles: 40°, 140°, 140°.
questions.explanation: Uses both vertically-opposite-angles-are-equal and linear-pair-sums-to-180° rules.

questions.question: Sketch (in words) one example each of: an acute angle, a right angle, an obtuse angle.
questions.answer: Acute: two arms making a narrow 'V' opening, like a partly closed pair of scissors (e.g. 30° opening). Right: two arms exactly perpendicular, forming a corner like a book (90°). Obtuse: two arms forming a wide 'V' opening greater than 90° but less than a straight line — like an open laptop lid at about 120°.
questions.explanation: Three named examples; rubric checks visual description matches the type.

questions.question: Two straight lines intersect. The angles formed are (in some order) (3x − 10)°, (x + 50)°, and two other angles. (i) Set up an equation using a linear pair. (ii) Find x. (iii) State all four angles.
questions.answer: (i) (3x − 10) and (x + 50) form a linear pair (one of the two pairs at the intersection): (3x − 10) + (x + 50) = 180. (ii) 4x + 40 = 180 → 4x = 140 → x = 35. (iii) Angles: 3(35) − 10 = 95°; 35 + 50 = 85°. Verify: 95 + 85 = 180 ✓. Vertically opposite angles repeat, so the four angles are 95°, 85°, 95°, 85°.
questions.explanation: Combine the linear-pair rule with algebra; check using vertical angles.

questions.question: Describe how you would use a protractor to draw each of these angles: (i) 60°, (ii) 90°, (iii) 135°. Outline your steps for each.
questions.answer: Common steps: draw an initial ray (one arm) ending at the vertex; place the protractor centre on the vertex; align the 0° line with the ray; mark a small dot at the desired degree; draw a ray from the vertex through the dot. Specifically: (i) 60° — mark at 60° on the scale; close to acute. (ii) 90° — mark at 90°; the dot lies straight up; this is a right angle (the second arm is perpendicular). (iii) 135° — mark at 135°; the second arm leans backwards past 90°; this is obtuse.
questions.explanation: Same procedure for all three; only the mark position differs. Correct scale (inner/outer) depends on which way the first arm points.
